note: Consumes attacker-controlled input bytes from the current lexer position.
A leading '/' is classified as division and forwarded into the division-token path.
The parser interprets the division token as the start of a regular-expression literal.
The regexp scanner must stop before lexer->end; malformed input can violate the expected bounded scan over the remaining bytes.
The scanner advances through the pattern and can read past the intended end while searching for the closing delimiter, triggering the heap-buffer-overflow.
